Last week, Bloomberg reported that Apple is developing a screenless fitness tracker, similar to WHOOP or Fitbit Air. I've been using WHOOP for the past six months and do think it's a good idea, but there are several areas where I hope Apple can do better.

Since the product is still in early development, we don't yet know the specific design of Apple's screenless fitness tracker. It may not launch until 2028 at the earliest. Bloomberg described it as a "slim fabric wristband with built-in sensors and computing modules."

Earlier this year, WHOOP partnered with Chase to offer a promotion allowing Sapphire credit card users to get a WHOOP device at a discount or for free — I was one of the beneficiaries. I started using WHOOP around then but have never been able to fully commit to it.

The reason is simple: automatic workout detection can never be perfect, and I find it cumbersome to have to pull out my phone to log a workout — whether before or after exercise. With Apple Watch, you can start tracking right from the watch face, and WHOOP can sync its time from Apple Health. That's the main reason I keep wearing my Apple Watch.

If I'm heading to the gym to work out, pulling out my phone is acceptable, but if I'm just casually cycling or going for a walk, I don't want the hassle of taking out my phone.

So for Apple's screenless fitness tracker, I really hope to see some kind of button-plus-indicator-light combo to start and stop workout recording. You'd still need your phone afterward to categorise the activity type, but I'd rather do that afterwards than during the workout. Apple could also develop classification models based on various factors.

Summary

If Apple can successfully create a screenless fitness tracker that doesn't feel cumbersome and doesn't rely on a phone, I think it would be quite appealing. This kind of design has several benefits, including being more comfortable to wear, longer battery life, and being able to wear it alongside a traditional watch.

Personally, after evaluating WHOOP, I actually prefer to just wear a smartwatch, even if it means sacrificing battery life. I understand some people want a screenless design to avoid distractions, but for me, simply turning on the watch's Do Not Disturb mode already solves that problem.

What are your thoughts on Apple developing a screenless fitness tracker? How much would you be willing to pay for it? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
